hook.situation: You are going to a Korean coworker's 집들이. You need to choose a practical gift, use a safe title, read the room, offer help politely, and thank people without sounding too casual.
objectives: Choose and explain housewarming gifts with 집들이, 선물, 휴지, and 세제.
Handle age and titles with 나이, 동갑, 선배/후배, 호칭, and 어르신.
Use 눈치, 도와드리다, 챙기다, 수고하셨습니다, and 덕분에 in socially careful sentences.
hook.whyItMatters: Korean social customs are not just facts about culture. They show up as sentence choices: what gift you bring, what title you use, when you offer help, and how you thank someone afterward.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-잖아요 - you know, this is shared
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use 잖아요 when you treat the reason as something the listener already recognizes.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach 잖아요 to a verb, adjective, or noun with 이잖아요. It reminds the listener of shared information, so it can sound warm among friends but pushy if the listener did not know it. In this chapter, use it for widely recognized social habits: 집들이 선물, title caution, and reading the room.

examples.ko: 집들이 선물로 휴지나 세제를 많이 가져가잖아요.
examples.romanization: jipdeuri seonmullo hyujina sejereul manhi gajyeogajanhayo.
examples.en: People often bring toilet paper or detergent as housewarming gifts, you know.
When people first meet, they are careful with titles, you know.
In front of elders, you are more careful with your tone, you know.

examples.ko: 분위기가 어색하면 먼저 물어보는 게 낫잖아요.
examples.romanization: bunwigiga eosaekamyeon meonjeo mureoboneun ge natjanhayo.
examples.en: If the mood is awkward, asking first is better, you know.
examples.note: 잖아요 can soften advice when the idea is shared.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-거든요 - here is the background
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use 거든요 when the listener needs background before your request or explanation makes sense.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach 거든요 to a verb or adjective, and use 이거든요 after a noun. It gives new background information, unlike 잖아요, which points to shared knowledge. At a 집들이, it lets you explain why you are asking about gifts, titles, or help.

examples.en: It is my first Korean housewarming, you see.
examples.note: New background before asking for advice.

examples.ko: 아직 어떤 호칭을 써야 할지 모르거든요.
examples.romanization: ajik eotteon hochingeul sseoya halji moreugeodeunyo.
examples.en: I still do not know what title I should use.
There will be elders there too, you see.
I bought detergent as the gift, you see.
examples.note: Gives background before checking if it is okay.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-는데요 - soften a careful question
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 는데요 lets you put a concern on the table without sounding blunt.
grammarNotes.formation: Verbs take 는데요, adjectives take ㄴ데요/은데요, and 있다/없다 take 는데요. In social situations it often means 'here is the situation, so...' and invites the other person to advise you.

examples.en: It is my first housewarming, so what gift is good?
I am not sure about the title, though.
examples.note: Leaves room for the listener to help.

examples.en: I would like to help, though.
The atmosphere feels a little awkward, though.
examples.note: 어색하다 is an adjective, so 어색한데요.

grammarNotes.title: V-(으)ㄴ/는 편이다 - I tend to / I am on the cautious side
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 편이다 softens a self-description so it does not sound absolute or boastful.
grammarNotes.formation: Verbs take 는 편이다, and adjectives take ㄴ/은 편이다. In social customs, this is useful for describing habits: 조심하는 편이에요, 챙기는 편이에요, 먼저 물어보는 편이에요. It sounds more modest than saying I always do this.

examples.en: At first, I tend to be careful with titles.
I tend to prepare a housewarming gift.

examples.ko: 선배 앞에서는 말을 먼저 놓지 않는 편이에요.
examples.romanization: seonbae apeseoneun mareul meonjeo nochi anneun pyeonieyo.
examples.en: In front of seniors, I tend not to switch to casual speech first.
I tend to read the room, so I ask first.

grammarNotes.title: V(으)니까 - since this is the situation
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use 니까 when your reason leads to advice, a request, or a next action.
grammarNotes.formation: Add 니까 after a vowel stem and 으니까 after a consonant stem. It often comes before suggestions or requests: 집들이니까 선물을 챙기세요, 어르신도 계시니까 조심하세요. Compared with 아/어서, 니까 is stronger for giving advice or explaining why someone should do something.

examples.en: Since it is a housewarming, prepare at least a small gift.
Since elders will be there too, be careful with titles.

examples.ko: 분위기가 어색하니까 먼저 도와드릴까요? 하고 물어보세요.
examples.romanization: bunwigiga eosaekanikka meonjeo dowadeurilkkayo? hago mureoboseyo.
examples.en: Since the mood is awkward, ask first, 'May I help?'

examples.ko: 선배님 덕분에 잘 됐으니까 감사 인사를 하세요.
examples.romanization: seonbaenim deokbune jal dwaesseunikka gamsa insareul haseyo.
examples.en: Since it went well thanks to your senior, say thank you.

grammarNotes.title: A/V-지만 - contrast with social care
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 지만 lets you admit one fact while still choosing the socially careful action.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach 지만 directly to a verb or adjective stem. For nouns, use 이지만/지만. It gives a clean contrast: 동갑이지만, 어색하지만, 바쁘지만. In this chapter the second clause usually shows the careful choice.

examples.en: We are the same age, but at first I use polite speech.
examples.note: Age does not automatically mean casual speech.

examples.en: It is a little awkward, but I will ask first.
I am busy, but I prepared the housewarming gift.

examples.ko: 친하지 않지만 선배님이라고 부르는 게 안전해요.
examples.romanization: chinhaji anchiman seonbaenimirago bureuneun ge anjeonhaeyo.
examples.en: We are not close, but calling them seonbaenim is safe.

exampleSentence.en: I am going to a senior coworker's housewarming this weekend.
It is okay to bring detergent as a housewarming gift.
People often bring toilet paper as a housewarming gift, you know.
I bought detergent as the housewarming gift, you see.
If your ages are similar, you might be the same age.
We are the same age, but at first I use polite speech.
At first, I tend to call them seonbaenim.
Even with a junior, it is good to use polite speech at first.
If elders are there too, be careful with your tone.

exampleSentence.ko: 눈치 있게 챙기면 분위기가 덜 어색해요.
exampleSentence.en: If you take care of things tactfully, the mood is less awkward.
If the atmosphere is awkward, ask first.
It is a little awkward because it is the first meeting.

extendedVocabulary.english: thank you for your hard work

exampleSentence.en: Thank you for inviting me today. Thank you for your hard work.
Thanks to you, the atmosphere became comfortable.

extendedDialogue.setting: Minseo asks how to behave at a coworker's housewarming.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 집들이에 갈 때 휴지랑 세제 중에 뭐가 나아요?
lines.romanization: jipdeurie gal ttae hyujirang seje junge mwoga naayo?
lines.en: When going to a housewarming, which is better, toilet paper or detergent?
lines.grammarNote: V(으)ㄹ 때 sets the social situation.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 둘 다 괜찮아요. 집들이 선물로 많이 가져가잖아요.
lines.romanization: dul da gwaenchanayo. jipdeuri seonmullo manhi gajyeogajanhayo.
lines.en: Both are fine. People often bring them as housewarming gifts, you know.
lines.grammarNote: 잖아요 treats the custom as shared knowledge.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: If we are about the same age, can I say we are the same age?

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 그래도 처음엔 선배님 같은 호칭을 쓰는 편이에요.
lines.romanization: geuraedo cheoeumen seonbaenim gateun hochingeul sseuneun pyeonieyo.
lines.en: Even so, at first people tend to use a title like seonbaenim.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: If elders are there too, I will ask, 'May I help?'
lines.grammarNote: 계시다 and 도와드리다 keep the respectful tone.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 좋아요. 눈치 있게 챙기면 분위기가 덜 어색해요.
lines.romanization: joayo. nunchi itge chaenggimyeon bunwigiga deol eosaekaeyo.
lines.en: Good. If you take care of things tactfully, the mood is less awkward.

readingText.title: 집들이에서 호칭과 눈치 챙기기
readingText.body: 민서는 회사 선배 집들이에 가려고 해요. 집들이 선물로 휴지와 세제 중에서 고민하다가, 실용적인 세제를 사기로 했어요. 처음 만나는 사람들이 있을 수 있으니까 나이와 호칭도 조심하려고 해요. 나이가 비슷해 보여도 바로 반말하지 않고, 처음에는 선배님 같은 호칭을 쓰는 편이에요. 어르신도 계시면 먼저 도와드릴까요? 하고 물어볼 거예요. 분위기가 어색하면 눈치 있게 선물을 건네고, 마지막에는 초대해 주셔서 감사합니다, 덕분에 편했어요라고 말하려고 해요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Minseo is going to a senior coworker's housewarming. After thinking between toilet paper and detergent as a housewarming gift, Minseo decided to buy practical detergent. Since there may be people Minseo is meeting for the first time, Minseo plans to be careful with age and titles too. Even if someone seems close in age, Minseo will not switch to casual speech right away and tends to use a title like seonbaenim at first. If elders are there, Minseo will ask first, 'May I help?' If the atmosphere feels awkward, Minseo will give the gift tactfully and at the end say, 'Thank you for inviting me. I felt comfortable thanks to you.'

comprehensionQuestions.question: 민서는 집들이 선물로 무엇을 사기로 했어요?
나이가 비슷해 보여도 처음에는 어떻게 해요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 바로 반말하지 않고 선배님 같은 호칭을 쓰는 편이에요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 마지막에 어떤 감사 표현을 하려고 해요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 초대해 주셔서 감사합니다, 덕분에 편했어요라고 말하려고 해요.

culturalNote.title: 눈치는 말보다 타이밍
culturalNote.body: 눈치 is often translated as reading the room, but at a gathering it becomes timing: when to ask, when to help, when to stay quiet, and when to thank someone. At a 집들이, the safe pattern is simple. Bring a practical 선물, use a respectful 호칭 until the relationship is clear, ask before helping, and close with a warm 감사 expression such as 덕분에 편했어요.
culturalNote.tip: If you are unsure, combine a soft sentence ending with a respectful verb: 호칭을 잘 모르는데요, 어떻게 부르면 될까요?

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence naturally explains a housewarming gift custom?
options: 집들이 선물로 휴지나 세제를 많이 가져가잖아요.
inlineExercises.correct: 집들이 선물로 휴지나 세제를 많이 가져가잖아요.
inlineExercises.explanation: 선물로 marks the role, and 잖아요 points to a familiar custom.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence is safest when you do not know the title?
inlineExercises.explanation: Asking about 호칭 is safer than guessing too casually.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence thanks someone with a positive cause?
inlineExercises.explanation: 덕분에 is the warm positive-cause expression for gratitude.

bullets: Housewarming set: 집들이, 선물, 휴지, 세제, 챙기다.
Title set: 나이, 동갑, 선배/후배, 호칭, 어르신.
Room-reading set: 눈치, 분위기, 어색하다, 도와드리다, 수고하셨습니다.
Gratitude set: 덕분에 is for positive causes; 때문에 can sound like blame.
